\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Basic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Basic
\section{Overview}
Affine hypercontractivity is defined for real random variables and extended norm exponents. Symmetric and Rademacher laws, finite atom support, multilinear evaluation, and moment identities provide the common probability-space framework.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Affine hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\leanok
For a real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and extended exponents $p,q\in[0,\infty]$, $(p,q,\rho)$-hypercontractivity means $1\le p\le q$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for every $a,b\in\bbr$, with extended-valued norms and the essential supremum at infinity.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real-valued random-variable norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\leanok
For a real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $q\in\bbr$, define $N_q(X)$ by taking the extended norm at exponent $\max(q,0)$ and converting it to a real number; a finite value is retained and an infinite value is assigned $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsSymmetricRV}
\leanok
A real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ is symmetric when $X$ and $-X$ are almost everywhere measurable and have the same distribution under $\mu$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rademacher random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV}
\leanok
A Rademacher variable on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ is a measurable $r:\Omega\to\bbr$ satisfying $r\in\{-1,1\}$ almost everywhere and $\mu(r=1)=\mu(r=-1)=1/2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Random-input multilinear evaluation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
Let $F$ assign a real coefficient $F(S)$ to every $S\subseteq[n]$, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\bbr$. Define $F(X)(\omega)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i(\omega)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lower bounds on finite atoms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound}
\leanok
A real function $X$ on $(\Omega,\mu)$ has atom lower bound $\lambda\in\bbr$ when there exists a finite $s\subseteq\bbr$ supporting $X$ almost everywhere and every $x\in s$ satisfies $\mu(X=x)\ge\max(\lambda,0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Power of a finite random-variable norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $q>0$ and $X\in L^q(\mu)$ on an arbitrary measure space. Its finite real norm satisfies $\|X\|_q^q=\int|X|^q\,d\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second norm of a centered affine function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_affine_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X\in L^2(\mu)$ satisfy $\E X=0$, and let $a,b\in\bbr$. Then $\|a+bX\|_2^2=a^2+b^2\|X\|_2^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Law of a Rademacher variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV.map_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ be a measurable random variable on a probability space, with $r\in\{-1,1\}$ almost surely and $\Pr[r=1]=\Pr[r=-1]=1/2$. Its law is $\tfrac12\delta_1+\tfrac12\delta_{-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conjugate affine contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.conjugate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\difficulty{6}
Let $X$ be centered on a probability space, let $q>2$, and suppose $H_{2,q,\rho}(X)$. Then $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho}(X)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling preserves affine hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ be a real function on an arbitrary measure space, suppose $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$, and let $c\in\bbr$. Then $H_{p,q,\rho}(cX)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reducing the contraction radius]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.mono_radius}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\difficulty{6}
Let $X$ be centered on a probability space, suppose $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$, and let $0\le\sigma\le\rho$. Then $H_{p,q,\sigma}(X)$, including extended exponents equal to infinity. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite support gives every finite norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound.memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure and $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ measurable. If a finite set supports $X$ almost everywhere and each listed value has mass at least $\max(\lambda,0)$ for some real $\lambda$, then $X\in L^p(\mu)$ for every $p\in[0,\infty]$, including essential boundedness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moments of multilinear evaluations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each belonging to $L^4$. For arbitrary real coefficients $F(S)$, the multilinear evaluation $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ belongs to $L^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Algebraic fourth-moment recurrence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reasonable_moment_algebra}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $R,a,b,A,D,C\in\bbr$ satisfy $R\ge9$, $a,b,C,D\ge0$, $A\le Ra^2$, $D\le b^2$, and $C^2\le AD$. Then $A+6C+RD\le R(a+b)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Splitting a multilinear sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.multilinear_sum_insert}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s$ be a finite subset of an index set $I$, let $i\notin s$, let $F$ assign real coefficients to finite subsets of $I$, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\bbr$. For every $\omega\in\Omega$, $\sum_{T\subseteq s\cup\{i\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)=\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)+X_i(\omega)\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T\cup\{i\})\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of mixed powers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure, let $p,a,b\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $a+b\le p$, and let real functions $f,g\in L^p(\mu)$. Then $f^ag^b$ is integrable.
\end{theorem}
